According to the latest issue of the *Power On* newsletter, Apple has been considering adding a feature to the Apple Upgrade programme that would make setting up an iPhone almost seamless: Apple would pre-load your data onto the new device. However, the feature never came to fruition.

The concept is simple: since users upgrade their devices on a regular monthly payment plan, why not make the switch as painless as possible? Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports:

There are clearly some issues with this. First, your iCloud backup would be slightly out of date, since the data transfer can only happen at the time of shipment, which would be a few days behind — unless you choose to pick up in store.

On top of that, there are obvious privacy concerns. If you already use iCloud backups, the fact that Apple has your data shouldn't come as a surprise. But for the general public, there could be concerns about how the data is transferred to the new phone, and whether anyone could peek at it along the way.

Two years ago, Apple launched a new system in its retail stores called Presto, which allows staff to update the software on an iPhone while it's still in its box. It's conceivable that this system could later be extended to support iCloud backup transfers, with no one ever needing to touch your data.

Still, the feature never launched, and that might be for the better.
